title: XML parsers should not be vulnerable to XXE attacks
description: XML External Entity (XXE) attacks exploit vulnerabilities in XML parsers that process external entity references. When XML parsers are configured to resolve external entities, attackers can inject malicious XML that references external files, URLs, or system resources. This can lead to sensitive file disclosure, server-side request forgery (SSRF), denial of service attacks, and in some cases remote code execution. XML parsers should be configured securely to disable external entity processing and other dangerous features.
message: Make sure this XML parser is not vulnerable to XXE attacks.
impact: XXE vulnerabilities can lead to sensitive information disclosure (reading local files, internal network scanning), denial of service attacks (billion laughs attack, quadratic blowup), server-side request forgery (SSRF), and potentially remote code execution. Attackers can access configuration files, source code, databases, and other sensitive resources on the server.
recommendation: Disable external entity processing in XML parsers by setting appropriate security flags. Use secure parser configurations such as disabling DTD processing, external entity resolution, and network access. Consider using defusedxml library for additional security or configure standard parsers with secure settings.

references.title: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XXE Reference

noncompliant.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import xml.dom.minidom as minidom
from xml.sax import make_parser
import lxml.etree as etree

# Vulnerable: Default xml.etree.ElementTree configuration
def parse_xml_vulnerable1(xml_data):
    root = ET.fromstring(xml_data)  # Vulnerable to XXE
    return root

# Vulnerable: xml.dom.minidom without security settings
def parse_xml_vulnerable2(xml_file):
    dom = minidom.parse(xml_file)  # Vulnerable to XXE
    return dom

# Vulnerable: SAX parser without security configuration
def parse_xml_vulnerable3(xml_file):
    parser = make_parser()  # Vulnerable to XXE
    parser.parse(xml_file)

# Vulnerable: lxml with default settings
def parse_xml_vulnerable4(xml_data):
    parser = etree.XMLParser()  # Vulnerable to XXE
    root = etree.fromstring(xml_data, parser)
    return root

# Vulnerable: iterparse without protection
def parse_xml_vulnerable5(xml_file):
    for event, elem in ET.iterparse(xml_file):  # Vulnerable to XXE
        process_element(elem)
noncompliant.description: XML parsers using default configurations that allow external entity processing, making them vulnerable to XXE attacks.

compliant.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import xml.dom.minidom as minidom
from xml.sax import make_parser
from xml.sax.handler import feature_external_ges, feature_external_pes
import lxml.etree as etree
import defusedxml.ElementTree as safe_ET
import defusedxml.minidom as safe_minidom

# Secure: Using defusedxml (recommended)
def parse_xml_secure1(xml_data):
    root = safe_ET.fromstring(xml_data)
    return root

def parse_xml_secure2(xml_file):
    dom = safe_minidom.parse(xml_file)
    return dom

# Secure: Configuring standard parsers safely
def parse_xml_secure3(xml_data):
    # Create XMLParser with security settings
    parser = ET.XMLParser()
    # Disable external entity processing
    parser.entity = {}
    root = ET.fromstring(xml_data, parser)
    return root

# Secure: lxml with security configuration
def parse_xml_secure4(xml_data):
    parser = etree.XMLParser(
        resolve_entities=False,  # Disable entity resolution
        no_network=True,        # Disable network access
        dtd_validation=False,   # Disable DTD validation
        load_dtd=False         # Don't load DTD
    )
    root = etree.fromstring(xml_data, parser)
    return root

# Secure: SAX parser with security features disabled
def parse_xml_secure5(xml_file):
    parser = make_parser()
    parser.setFeature(feature_external_ges, False)  # Disable external general entities
    parser.setFeature(feature_external_pes, False)  # Disable external parameter entities
    parser.parse(xml_file)

# Secure: Using iterparse with custom parser
def parse_xml_secure6(xml_file):
    parser = etree.XMLParser(
        resolve_entities=False,
        no_network=True,
        dtd_validation=False,
        load_dtd=False
    )
    for event, elem in etree.iterparse(xml_file, parser=parser):
        process_element(elem)
compliant.description: Secure XML parsing using defusedxml library or properly configured standard parsers with external entity processing disabled.

devsecops.security: Critical - Prevents file disclosure, SSRF, and DoS attacks
devsecops.automation: High - Can be automatically detected through parser configuration analysis
devsecops.compliance: Critical - Addresses OWASP Top 10, CWE, and PCI DSS requirements

why_is_this_an_issue: XXE vulnerabilities occur when XML parsers process external entity references without proper security controls. Attackers can craft malicious XML documents that reference external files (file:// scheme), internal network resources (http:// scheme), or use recursive entity definitions to cause denial of service. This can lead to unauthorized file access, network scanning, credential theft, and system compromise. The vulnerability is particularly dangerous because it can be exploited through any XML input processed by the application, including configuration files, data imports, and API requests.
how_to_fix: 1. Use the defusedxml library instead of standard XML parsers for maximum security. 2. If using standard parsers, disable external entity processing by setting resolve_entities=False, no_network=True, and load_dtd=False. 3. For xml.sax parsers, disable external general entities and parameter entities using setFeature(). 4. Validate and sanitize XML input before parsing. 5. Use allowlists for acceptable XML content and schemas. 6. Implement proper error handling to avoid information disclosure. 7. Keep XML parsing libraries updated to the latest versions.
